If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over last 5 days, adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to reflect overconfidence bias.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) over last 5 days, adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to counteract pessimism-induced underestimation.

If sentiment spikes to 1.00 on day 1 of forecast window, reduce forecast by 1.0–2.0% for late horizon (16–30 days) to account for sentiment-driven overreaction.

If sentiment alternates sharply between 0.00 and 1.00 over last 3 days, apply a 0.5–1.0% smoothing correction to forecast mid-point to avoid volatility overfitting.

If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is trending upward, add 0.3–0.7% upward bias to forecast for late horizon to capture sentiment lag effect.

If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is trending downward, add 0.3–0.7% downward bias to forecast for early horizon to prevent sentiment-induced overcorrection.
